invariant: A bracket inside a sequence arrow is one ordered arrow-configuration expression, not a color literal. CommandArrow captures the complete bracket body independently of the arrow shaft and applies it after deriving the shaft's base body, heads, direction, and decorations. CommandArrow.applyStyle tokenizes the body on commas. At the pinned Java revision, `dashed` and `dotted` select ArrowBody.DOTTED, `hidden` selects ArrowBody.HIDDEN, `bold` is accepted without changing the configuration, and every other accepted token is resolved as a color; later tokens operate on the configuration produced by earlier tokens. Color and body are therefore orthogonal and survive together for ordinary, self, reversed, bidirectional, and external sequence messages. The bracket is part of the arrow header only, so Creole anchors such as `[[#anchor label]]` in message text are not arrow styles.
causal_divergence: Rust's strip_arrow_color_annotation recognizes only bracket bodies beginning with `#`, captures every remaining token as part of one color string, and removes the bracket before parse_arrow sees the shaft. For `-[#C2185B,dashed]>`, the parser stores color `#C2185B,dashed` and leaves LineStyle::Solid. The renderer then passes that invalid compound to resolve_color, producing #FFFFFF, and emits a solid line. The preserved review5_sequence_repeated_theme_cross_family_alias counterexample isolates this loss: inherited arrows already match Java's #2E7D32, while only the local arrow differs as Java #C2185B dashed versus Rust #FFFFFF solid. External-message parsing discards the captured bracket entirely, exposing the same missing model on another command path. A direct parser correction made ordinary, self, reverse, and bidirectional perturbations exact but exposed an earlier dispatch loss for external messages: detect_uml_subtype treats `[dotted,#color]` and `[hidden]` in found/lost arrow headers as component-reference brackets and does not count the interrupted shaft as a sequence arrow. A valid source with explicit participants is consequently dispatched as DESCRIPTION before SequenceParser can apply the correct style model. This divergence is independent of theme alias precedence and participant geometry.
planned_change: Replace color-only stripping with a structured sequence-arrow-style parser that extracts at most one bracket expression from the arrow header before the message colon, removes only that expression from the shaft syntax, and applies comma-separated tokens in source order to the parsed Arrow. Preserve color and line body as separate fields. Map dashed and dotted to the existing dotted body, represent hidden explicitly so rendering suppresses the shaft and decorations while retaining the message event semantics Java preserves, accept bold as the pinned Java no-op, and resolve the remaining accepted token as the color with later color tokens winning. Use the same helper for ordinary and external messages. Expose the exact header recognizer to UML subtype detection: recognized inline sequence styles are sequence-arrow evidence and must be excluded from component bracket scoring, while unrelated `[Component]` syntax remains unchanged. Keep Creole label brackets outside the header untouched. Verify renamed ordinary, self, reversed, bidirectional, found, and lost messages; color-first and style-first token order; repeated color tokens; inherited skinparam controls; and message labels containing local Creole anchors. Do not special-case the review label, theme names, participant count, or rendered coordinates.
